questions.stem: A learner completes 3/4 of a review on Monday and half of the remaining work on Tuesday. What fraction is still unfinished?
questions.why: One quarter remains after Monday. Half of that quarter is one eighth. Apply the second fraction to the remainder, not the whole.

questions.stem: A mixture uses concentrate and water in a 1:4 ratio. How much concentrate is needed for 750 mL of mixture?
questions.why: There are five equal parts in the final mixture. 750 ÷ 5 = 150 mL of concentrate; the other four parts are water.

questions.stem: How many milliliters equal 0.075 L?
questions.why: Multiply liters by 1,000: 0.075 × 1,000 = 75 mL. The smaller unit gives a larger number.

questions.stem: Solve 3(x − 2) = 21.
questions.why: Divide both sides by 3 to get x − 2 = 7. Add 2: x = 9. Substituting 9 gives 3 × 7 = 21.

questions.stem: Which chamber pumps blood directly into the pulmonary trunk?
questions.why: The right ventricle sends blood toward the lungs. The left ventricle pumps into the aorta.

questions.stem: Why does oxygen move from the alveoli into pulmonary capillary blood?
options: Higher oxygen partial pressure in alveoli
Oxygen follows carbon dioxide in the same direction
questions.why: Oxygen diffuses down its partial-pressure gradient. Carbon dioxide has its own gradient, in the opposite direction.

questions.stem: Read: “A class replaced one long review with three short sessions. Students recalled more after a week, although their immediate scores were similar. The teacher kept the shorter sessions.” Which statement best captures the main idea?
options: Short sessions improved delayed recall in this class
questions.why: The passage contrasts similar immediate scores with better later recall. The other choices add claims the passage does not support.

questions.stem: Read: “The library extended evening hours during exam week. Every evening, the additional study rooms filled within an hour.” Which inference is best supported?
options: There was demand for evening study space
questions.why: Quickly filled rooms support demand for space. The passage says nothing about fees, home study, or exam outcomes.

questions.stem: “The patient's symptoms were transient and resolved before the appointment.” In this sentence, transient means:
questions.why: Transient means short-lived. The phrase about symptoms resolving supports that meaning.

questions.stem: Which term means occurring on both sides?
questions.why: Bilateral refers to both sides. Unilateral is one-sided; proximal and distal describe relative distance.

questions.stem: After removing gloves, a nurse sees blood on their hands. What should happen next?
options: Apply a second pair of gloves
Use gloves instead of hand hygiene
questions.why: Visible blood requires soap and water. Gloves do not replace cleaning the hands.

questions.stem: Which actions belong to Standard Precautions? Select all that apply.
options: Use eye protection when a splash is anticipated
Reuse a syringe after changing the needle
questions.why: Standard Precautions include hand hygiene, exposure-appropriate protection, and equipment cleaning. A new needle does not make a used syringe safe.

questions.stem: A nurse has a single-dose vial with medication left over after treating one patient. Which plan is appropriate?
options: Combine it with another opened vial
Use it for another patient with a new syringe
questions.why: Single-dose vials are for one patient. Leftover medication should not become a shared supply.

questions.stem: A procedure is expected to splash body fluid toward the nurse's face. Which preparation addresses that risk?
options: Eye and face protection appropriate to the exposure
Hand hygiene after the procedure only
questions.why: Choose protective equipment for the anticipated exposure. Gloves alone do not protect the eyes, nose, or mouth.

questions.stem: A patient taking warfarin reports black, tarry stools. Which response has priority?
options: Explain this is an expected harmless effect
Promptly assess and contact the treating clinician about possible bleeding
Wait for the next routine INR appointment
questions.why: Tarry stools can indicate bleeding. This needs prompt assessment and escalation, rather than waiting for a routine laboratory visit.

questions.stem: Which statements show appropriate warfarin teaching? Select all that apply.
options: Double the next dose after a missed day
Discuss new supplements with the pharmacist or prescriber
Keep vitamin K intake reasonably consistent
questions.why: Monitoring and interaction checks matter. Vitamin K intake should be consistent, and a missed dose is not corrected by doubling the next day's dose.

questions.stem: After starting furosemide, a patient reports marked thirst, weakness, and muscle cramps. What should the nurse prioritize?
options: Treat the symptoms as proof the medication is working
Assess fluid and electrolyte status and notify the clinician
Tell the patient to avoid all fluids
questions.why: These symptoms may signal excessive fluid or electrolyte loss. Assess and escalate rather than changing the dose without an order.

questions.stem: A patient taking warfarin wants to start an over-the-counter ibuprofen product. What is the best response?
options: It is always safe because no prescription is needed
Check with the pharmacist or prescriber before starting it
questions.why: Ibuprofen can increase bleeding risk with warfarin. Nonprescription status does not remove the need to check an interaction.

questions.stem: A catheter passes from the right atrium through the tricuspid valve. Which chamber does it enter next?
questions.why: The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and right ventricle.

questions.stem: Blood leaving the left ventricle enters which vessel?
questions.why: The aorta carries left-ventricular output into systemic circulation.

questions.stem: During a cardiac follow-up, a patient taking warfarin describes a fall with a head strike. Which response is appropriate?
options: Wait to see whether a bruise appears
Reassure because there is no visible bleeding
questions.why: Head injury while taking an anticoagulant requires prompt medical attention. Absence of visible bleeding is not reassurance.

questions.stem: Which structures are atrioventricular valves? Select all that apply.
questions.why: Tricuspid and mitral valves separate atria from ventricles. Aortic and pulmonary valves are ventricular outflow valves.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: an order is 750 mg. Each tablet contains 250 mg. How many tablets supply the ordered amount?
questions.why: 750 mg ÷ 250 mg per tablet = 3 tablets. Units cancel to tablets.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: a solution contains 125 mg per 5 mL. What volume contains 300 mg?
Calculation exercise: 1,000 mL must run over 8 hours. What rate in mL/hour gives that volume?
questions.why: Divide volume by hours: 1,000 ÷ 8 = 125 mL/hour.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: a 44-lb child has an order for 10 mg/kg per dose. Use 2.2 lb = 1 kg. What is the dose?
questions.why: 44 ÷ 2.2 = 20 kg. Then 20 kg × 10 mg/kg = 200 mg per dose. A real medication also needs dose-range checks.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: 30 mg/kg/day is divided into three equal doses for a 20-kg patient. What is each dose?
questions.why: The total daily amount is 30 × 20 = 600 mg. Divide by three doses: 200 mg per dose.

questions.stem: A parent asks how to position an infant for routine sleep. Which response is appropriate?
options: On the back on a firm, flat sleep surface
On the side with a rolled blanket
questions.why: Use a firm, flat sleep surface and place the infant on their back.

questions.stem: Which choices support an infant's safe sleep environment? Select all that apply.
options: A fitted sheet on a firm sleep surface
Keeping soft toys out of the sleep space
Sharing a room on a separate sleep surface
questions.why: Keep the sleep space free of loose bedding and soft objects. Room sharing on a separate sleep surface is safer than bed sharing.

questions.stem: A parent says their child has lost a skill they previously used. What should the nurse encourage?
options: Wait until the next school year
Compare the child only with siblings
Promptly discuss the change with the child's healthcare professional
Assume every lost skill is normal
questions.why: Loss of a skill warrants a conversation and developmental follow-up. A milestone checklist is not a substitute for evaluation.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: a child weighs 33 lb. Using 2.2 lb = 1 kg, which weight should be used in a mg/kg calculation?
questions.why: 33 ÷ 2.2 = 15 kg. Convert pounds before applying a dose stated per kilogram.

questions.stem: Which pancreatic cells release insulin?
questions.why: Beta cells in pancreatic islets release insulin. Alpha cells release glucagon. Think of the cell type and its hormone as a pair.

questions.stem: Which division is most associated with the body's fight-or-flight response?
questions.why: The sympathetic division coordinates responses to challenge, including changes in heart activity. The parasympathetic division supports many rest-and-digest functions.

questions.stem: A patient taking warfarin realizes they forgot yesterday’s dose and it is now time for today’s dose. Which guidance is appropriate?
options: Take yesterday’s and today’s doses together now
Take today’s dose as usual and report the missed dose to the prescriber
Stop warfarin until the next INR appointment
questions.why: A missed warfarin dose is not made up by doubling. The usual dose continues and the prescriber is told, because the INR may need to be checked sooner.

questions.stem: Which report from a patient taking warfarin needs the most prompt follow-up?
options: A small bruise on the forearm after bumping a table
A nosebleed that has not stopped after 10 minutes of firm pressure
A preference for taking the dose in the evening
Eating a green salad twice a week
questions.why: Bleeding that does not stop with pressure is a warning sign on an anticoagulant. Minor bruising, evening dosing, and consistent vitamin K intake do not need urgent action.

questions.stem: A patient is starting furosemide. Which points belong in the teaching? Select all that apply.
options: Rise slowly from sitting to standing
Report muscle cramps or an irregular heartbeat
Take the dose at bedtime so the effect happens during sleep
Report ringing in the ears or a change in hearing
Expect to urinate more after each dose
questions.why: Furosemide can drop blood pressure on standing, lower potassium, and affect hearing. Increased urination is expected, which is why the dose is usually taken earlier in the day rather than at bedtime.

questions.stem: A patient taking furosemide has a potassium result below the reference range and reports leg cramps. Which action is most appropriate first?
options: Notify the prescriber and follow orders for potassium monitoring or replacement
Reassure the patient that cramps are expected
questions.why: Low potassium with symptoms is a medication effect that needs the prescriber’s decision. More diuretic would worsen it, and reassurance ignores a correctable problem.

questions.stem: A patient stabilized on warfarin is prescribed a new antibiotic. Which teaching is safest?
options: No change is needed because antibiotics do not affect warfarin
The INR may change, so expect closer monitoring and report any bleeding
Stop warfarin for the length of the antibiotic course
Double vitamin K intake while on the antibiotic
questions.why: Many medicines change how warfarin works. The safe response is closer INR monitoring and bleeding awareness, not stopping the anticoagulant or changing the diet on your own.

questions.stem: Which laboratory value is used to monitor warfarin therapy?
questions.why: Warfarin is dosed against the INR. Glucose and A1c track diabetes control, and potassium is watched with diuretics rather than with warfarin.

questions.stem: Oxygen-poor blood returning from the body enters the heart through which route?
options: Pulmonary veins into the left atrium
Superior and inferior venae cavae into the right atrium
Pulmonary trunk into the right ventricle
questions.why: Systemic venous blood returns through the venae cavae to the right atrium. The pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

questions.stem: Blood returning from the lungs enters which chamber first?
questions.why: The pulmonary veins deliver freshly oxygenated blood to the left atrium, which passes it through the mitral valve to the left ventricle.

questions.stem: Which valve sits between the left ventricle and the aorta?
questions.why: The aortic valve is the left ventricle’s outflow valve. The mitral valve is the left atrioventricular valve, and the tricuspid and pulmonary valves belong to the right side.

questions.stem: Which statements about the structure of the heart are accurate? Select all that apply.
options: The myocardium is the muscular layer that contracts
The endocardium lines the inside of the chambers
The pericardium is the innermost layer of the heart wall
The interventricular septum separates the two ventricles
questions.why: From the outside in, the layers are epicardium, myocardium, and endocardium. The pericardium is the sac around the heart, not a layer of the wall. The septum keeps right- and left-sided blood separate.

questions.stem: A cardiac patient taking warfarin asks whether to take aspirin for a headache. Which response is best?
options: Aspirin is fine in any amount
Check with the prescriber or pharmacist first because bleeding risk can increase
Take a double dose of aspirin so it works faster
Skip today’s warfarin and take the aspirin
questions.why: Aspirin adds antiplatelet effect to an anticoagulant, so bleeding risk rises. The prescriber decides; the patient should not skip warfarin or self-adjust.

questions.stem: Which vessels supply the heart muscle itself with oxygen-rich blood?
options: Coronary arteries branching from the aorta
questions.why: The coronary arteries arise from the base of the aorta and perfuse the myocardium. Blood inside the chambers does not nourish the heart wall.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: an order is 0.25 mg. Each tablet is labeled 125 mcg. How many tablets are needed?
questions.why: Convert first: 0.25 mg = 250 mcg. Then 250 ÷ 125 = 2 tablets. Match units before dividing.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: 500 mL must infuse over 4 hours with tubing that delivers 15 drops/mL. What is the rate in drops per minute?
questions.why: 500 mL ÷ 240 minutes ≈ 2.08 mL/min. Multiply by 15 drops/mL to get about 31 drops per minute.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: a solution contains 250 mg per 10 mL. The order is 100 mg. What volume is needed?
questions.why: Set up the proportion: 100 mg × (10 mL ÷ 250 mg) = 4 mL.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: a patient weighs 66 lb. The order is 5 mg/kg. Using 2.2 lb = 1 kg, what is the dose?
questions.why: 66 ÷ 2.2 = 30 kg. Then 30 kg × 5 mg/kg = 150 mg. Convert pounds to kilograms before applying the dose.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: 750 mL is infusing at 125 mL/hour. How long will the infusion run?
questions.why: Divide volume by rate: 750 ÷ 125 = 6 hours.

questions.stem: A nurse’s hands are not visibly soiled after routine patient contact. Which hand hygiene method is appropriate?
options: Skip hand hygiene until hands look dirty
Wipe hands with a dry paper towel
questions.why: Alcohol-based hand rub is the preferred method when hands are not visibly soiled. Hand hygiene is still required after every patient contact.

questions.stem: A patient in the waiting area is coughing frequently. Which action reflects respiratory hygiene under Standard Precautions?
options: Ask the patient to leave the building
Offer a mask and tissues and encourage hand hygiene
Place every patient in the area in isolation
Take no action because coughing is common
questions.why: Respiratory hygiene means source control: covering the cough, offering a mask, and cleaning hands. It protects others without overreacting.

questions.stem: After giving an injection, what should the nurse do with the used needle?
options: Recap it carefully and place it in the regular trash
Place it directly into a sharps container without recapping
Bend the needle so it cannot be reused
Leave it on the tray to dispose of later
questions.why: Used sharps go straight into a puncture-resistant sharps container. Recapping, bending, and delayed disposal are common causes of needlestick injuries.

questions.stem: Which practices are consistent with safe injection practices? Select all that apply.
options: Use a new needle and syringe for every injection
Use a single-dose vial for one patient only
Keep multi-dose vials in the immediate patient treatment area
Enter a vial with a new sterile needle and syringe each time
questions.why: Needles, syringes, and single-dose vials are single use. Multi-dose vials are kept away from the immediate patient treatment area to avoid contamination.

questions.stem: When removing personal protective equipment after care, which item is generally removed first?
questions.why: Gloves are the most contaminated item and come off first. The mask is removed last, after leaving the room and cleaning hands.

questions.stem: Which situation calls for soap and water rather than an alcohol-based hand rub?
options: Between tasks on the same patient
questions.why: Alcohol rub does not remove visible soil. Soap and water are also used after exposure to certain spore-forming organisms.

questions.stem: A caregiver asks where an infant should sleep during the first months. Which arrangement is recommended?
options: On a firm, flat surface in the caregiver’s room but not in the same bed
On a couch with pillows for support
questions.why: Room-sharing without bed-sharing is recommended. Couches, pillows, and seats are not safe sleep surfaces.

questions.stem: Which item is safe to have in an infant’s sleep space?
options: A fitted sheet on a firm mattress
questions.why: The sleep surface should be firm and flat with only a fitted sheet. Soft objects and loose bedding increase suffocation risk.

questions.stem: A parent worries that their 12-month-old is not yet babbling or pointing. Which guidance is best?
options: Wait until age 3 to see whether it improves
Discuss the concern with the child’s clinician now and ask about developmental screening
Compare the child with older siblings
Assume it is a temporary phase
questions.why: Concerns about milestones deserve early attention. Screening and early support matter more than waiting or comparing.

questions.stem: Which statements reflect current guidance on developmental milestones? Select all that apply.
options: Milestones are skills most children can do by a certain age
A missed milestone is a reason to talk with a clinician
Children always catch up without help
Caregivers should act early rather than wait and see
questions.why: Milestones are population norms, not deadlines, but a missed one is a reason to talk with a clinician. “They will catch up” is not a plan.

questions.stem: Calculation exercise: a child weighs 22 lb. The order is 15 mg/kg per dose. Using 2.2 lb = 1 kg, what is the dose?
questions.why: 22 ÷ 2.2 = 10 kg. Then 10 kg × 15 mg/kg = 150 mg per dose.

questions.stem: A caregiver says the infant sleeps better on the stomach. Which teaching is best?
options: Stomach sleeping is fine once the infant seems comfortable
Place the infant on the back for every sleep, including naps
Prop the infant on the side with pillows
questions.why: Back to sleep applies to every sleep, not just nighttime. Side positioning and props are not safe alternatives.

questions.stem: A student answered 45 of 60 questions correctly. What percentage is that?
questions.why: 45 ÷ 60 = 0.75, or 75%. Divide the part by the whole, then move the decimal two places.

questions.stem: What is 2.5 × 0.4?
questions.why: Multiply as whole numbers (25 × 4 = 100), then place two decimal places: 1.00.

questions.stem: How many grams are in 2.4 kilograms?
questions.why: One kilogram is 1,000 grams, so 2.4 kg = 2,400 g. Moving to a smaller unit makes the number larger.

questions.stem: A clinic sees 3 new patients for every 5 returning patients. If 40 patients are seen, how many are new?
questions.why: The ratio has 8 parts in total. 40 ÷ 8 = 5 per part, so new patients are 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.stem: Read: “Short daily walks improved mood scores in a study of office workers more than one long weekly workout did, even though total exercise time was equal.” What is the main idea?
options: Frequent shorter activity had a stronger effect on mood than the same time spent in one session
questions.why: The passage compares two ways of spending the same exercise time and reports that the frequent pattern helped mood more. The other options add claims the passage never makes.

questions.stem: Read: “The pharmacy closes at 6 p.m. on weekdays and is closed on weekends. Refills requested after 4 p.m. are ready the next business day.” When will a refill requested on Friday at 5 p.m. be ready?
questions.why: A request after 4 p.m. waits for the next business day. The pharmacy is closed Saturday and Sunday, so that is Monday.

questions.stem: Which term describes a condition that develops suddenly and lasts a short time?
questions.why: Acute means sudden and short-lived. Chronic is long-lasting, benign means not harmful, and latent means present but not yet active.

questions.stem: “The nurse noted the wound was not healing and looked for any impediment to recovery.” What does impediment mean?
questions.why: An impediment is something that blocks or slows progress. The sentence is about looking for what is getting in the way of healing.

questions.stem: Where does gas exchange between air and blood take place in the lungs?
questions.why: Alveoli are the thin-walled sacs where oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across to and from pulmonary capillaries. The airways above them only conduct air.

questions.stem: Which pancreatic hormone raises blood glucose between meals?
questions.why: Glucagon from the alpha cells signals the liver to release glucose. Insulin does the opposite, and cortisol comes from the adrenal cortex rather than the pancreas.

questions.stem: Which division of the autonomic nervous system slows the heart rate and promotes digestion?
questions.why: The parasympathetic division supports rest-and-digest functions. The sympathetic division drives fight-or-flight, and the somatic system controls skeletal muscle.
